correctness.rationale: Verified for 3-state threshold-one GHM on free path: the height gradient d(0,1)=1,d(1,0)=-1 and local excitation indicators give h_{t+1}(v)=max_{u in N[v]}h_t(u). By diameter D=n-1 the height has stabilized and no new excitation occurs after update D; states 1 and 2 vanish within two more steps, giving T<=n+1. New excitation at update D-1 can occur only at one endpoint, exactly when that endpoint is a strict maximum of initial height over all other vertices; both events disjoint. Reverse-state-word walks with strictly positive prefix heights satisfy stated 3-letter kernel equations; cancellation at the unique small formal root yields S(z)=(sqrt((1+z)/(1-3z))-1)/(2z) and EGF ordinary A(z)=sqrt((1+z)/(1-3z)). Algebraic singularity at 1/3 gives probability constant 2/(3 sqrt(3 pi n)); n=1 treated separately. Independently replayed full original-state transitions for n=1..9 and recovered 1,2,4,10,26,70,192,534,1500; examined independent transfer and max-plus source files, which are finite corroboration only.

Distinctive exact finite-path enumerator remains best-knowledge novel, not just a known table with no dynamical interpretation.

value.rationale: Exactly counting the configurations that attain the natural largest transient in an established three-state cellular automaton is a mathematically motivated complete extremal classification, with an exact n^-1/2 rare-event law. The answer is not arbitrary because maximal first-zero time is intrinsic to the model. Although the same integers were known in other enumerative forms, identifying the precise dynamical class is substantive.

limitations: The result does not classify intermediate extinction-time strata or infinite paths, cyclic boundaries, or other color counts.
The counted OEIS sequence itself and the general height lemma are not new; unindexed past matching interpretation remains priority risk.
